title: Monthly client review, privacy and your retention numbers

say: Your monthly client review, client privacy, and your retention numbers.
This is the video for module 3 of Client Relationship Management.
Out-of-date records are dangerous because they look reliable. You might remind a client to reorder after she told you she closed her shop.

panel.heading: A five-point record standard
items: Every client has a status and next action date
Every promise logged the day it is made

say: So keep five rules. Log orders within 24 hours. Leave no blank status or next action date. Keep notes dated and factual. Log every promise in a Promises tab the day you make it. And never market to anyone who asked you to stop.
A forgotten promise does more harm than not promising at all.

panel.heading: A five-point record standard
items: Every client has a status and next action date

say: Once a month, sort your clients by value, meaning how much she spends, and engagement, meaning how active she is.
Protect your big, active clients with a personal thank-you and first choice of new items.
Re-engage big clients who have gone quiet. Call or send a voice note, and ask honestly if your service still fits.
Grow active clients who buy small, by mentioning a related service that genuinely suits them.
And maintain small, inactive clients lightly, with an occasional update only if they agreed to receive one.
Zainab filters her tracker on the first Saturday of the month. Her average client spend is about 40,000 naira.
Hauwa and Esther spend well above that and are active. She sends them a thank-you voice note and first choice of December slots.
Blessing spent 64,000 but has not come for 4 months, against a usual 6 weeks. She gets a personal voice note before she is lost for good.
Aisha and Mary come monthly for cornrows, and their records show they wear wigs at weekends. So Zainab mentions her wig revamp service.
She also finds a promised free scalp treatment for Esther in her Promises tab, and books it. One clear action for each client, in about 30 minutes.

Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 sets principles for anyone who uses personal data. Collect details only to serve the client, use them only for that, keep them accurate and secure, and do not keep them forever.

say: Saying yes to everything leads to late deliveries and broken promises. For example, Bisi cooks small chops in Ibadan. She has about 30 working hours a week, and a party order takes about 5 hours.

panel.heading: Bisi works out her weekly capacity
items: One party order takes about 5 hours
30 divided by 5 is 6 orders a week
Keep 1 slot free for repeat clients

say: So her maximum is 6 orders a week.

panel.heading: Bisi works out her weekly capacity
items: One party order takes about 5 hours
30 divided by 5 is 6 orders a week
Keep 1 slot free for repeat clients

say: She keeps 1 slot free for repeat clients' urgent requests. In a busy week, she politely offers extra requests the following week, or recommends a caterer she trusts. She keeps her quality and her promises.

panel.heading: Bisi works out her weekly capacity
items: One party order takes about 5 hours
30 divided by 5 is 6 orders a week
Keep 1 slot free for repeat clients

say: Feeling that clients are happy is not evidence. Numbers are. For example, Funmi supplies soap. She started January with 40 clients, gained 12 new ones, and ended March with 45 active.
Retention is clients at the end, minus new clients, divided by clients at the start. 45 minus 12 is 33. 33 divided by 40.
That is 82.5 percent. Most of the clients she started with stayed.
Churn is the opposite: 100 minus 82.5, which is 17.5 percent.
Her repeat rate is clients with 2 or more orders, divided by all clients. 29 of 52, about 56 percent.
Count honestly. Include clients who left unhappy. A modest true number that improves beats a perfect number nobody can check.

To remember. Keep clean records and a promises log. Review your four groups every month. Ask before marketing and honour every opt-out. Know your capacity. And track your numbers every quarter, including referrals from your Source column.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Log promises and keep records free of blanks
Know your capacity and say no kindly
Track retention, churn, repeat rate, referrals

say: Now practise. Add a Promises tab and sort every client into one of the four groups. Check your privacy settings, add a marketing consent column, and work out your weekly capacity. Then set your baseline retention, churn and repeat rate.
